subject: Burst credit carveout & price-smoothing amendment discussion
messages:
From: Jordan Cooper <jordan.cooper@acme.io>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme.io>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibit: burst credits + smoothing ask

Hi Dylan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and finance ran the pricing exhibit and have two items we need to get in writing before we sign: (1) a burst-credit carveout so we can absorb unexpected traffic spikes without being penalized by immediate true-up, and (2) a short-term price-smoothing mechanic for the first 3 billing periods to avoid volatility as we onboard users.

Specifically, our team proposed: a 10% burst credit bucket (used only for unanticipated traffic beyond committed QPS) with no retroactive surcharge for usage covered by that bucket, and a smoothing corridor that averages per-token effective price across months 1–3 for true-up calculations.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept carveout language and propose contract wording? We've attached a clean markup of Exhibit B with comments.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

— Jordan
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Jordan —

Thanks for the note and the redlines. Appreciate the clarity on the business need. Short answer: we can be flexible, but we need to balance unit economics and SLA exposure.

Next steps: I'll loop in legal and pricing ops. Marissa, Karthik — can you review Acme's proposed 10% burst bucket + 3-month smoothing and flag any operational/financial concerns? I'm attaching the doc they sent for reference.

If it helps, I'd like to propose alternative language that preserves the burst carveout but limits carry-forward true-up exposure to 1x of the burst bucket for the first quarter (instead of unlimited). Happy to explain on a quick call.

Talk soon —
Dylan

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: burst credits + smoothing ask (internal)

All —

Quick read on Acme's ask and my notes below:

- Burst bucket (10%): operationally implementable as a prefunded burst-credit ledger tied to the account. We can cap auto-use to unexpected horizontal scaling events (traffic spikes >150% of committed QPS for >5 minutes).

- No retro surcharge for usage within the burst bucket: acceptable, but need to limit how much can roll over. I'd propose we allow unused burst credits to expire after the quarter, and any usage beyond the burst bucket is subject to standard true-up.

- 3-month smoothing: reasonable, but it exposes Redwood to multi-month undercollection if Acme spikes then drops. To mitigate we should: (a) apply smoothing only to effective per-token price (not discounts tied to volume tiers), and (b) limit smoothing benefit to a max of 12% effective price reduction relative to the month-to-month baseline.

- Proposed contract language (draft bullets):
  * "Burst Credit" means a quarterly allocation equal to 10% of the committed token volume for the quarter. Burst Credits may be applied only to usage arising from traffic above 150% of Customer's committed QPS and used within the quarter in which they are allocated.
  * Unused Burst Credits expire at quarter-end and are not refundable. Usage beyond the Burst Credit allocation is subject to the pricing True-Up.
  * "Price Smoothing" applies only to the True-Up calculation for the first three billing periods following Contract Effective Date and shall be calculated as the average effective per-token price across such periods, subject to a ceiling equal to 112% of the baseline per-token price for month 1.

Karthik / Lauren — please review for legal and finance compliance. If this is acceptable I can prepare a redline PDF and an internal one-pager showing the worst-case collection delta for the quarter.

— Marissa
Senior Pricing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: burst credits + smoothing ask (internal)

Thanks Marissa —

I like the approach but suggest two guardrails to add to the language:

1) A usage telemetry clause requiring Acme to enable request-level telemetry and a shared reporting view for spikes that trigger Burst Credit consumption. This prevents disputes on what constitutes "unexpected traffic."

2) A quarterly reconciliation cap: limit Redwood's maximum undercollection exposure to 1.5x the total quarter's burst credit value. If reconciliation exceeds that cap, the parties will enter a 30-day remediation period during which additional backcharges are paused while engineering investigates.

I'll draft a one-paragraph legal-friendly clause to incorporate those two points and send it to Lauren for sign-off.

— Karthik
Principal Counsel, Revenue Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Cooper <jordan.cooper@acme.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: burst credits + smoothing ask

Jordan —

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed. Attached is a proposed redline (ACME_Pricing_Exhibit_v3_redline.pdf) and a short burst-smoothing-matrix showing example math for three onboarding profiles (low/medium/high). Summary of the compromise:

- We will provide a quarterly Burst Credit equal to 10% of committed volume. Burst Credits apply only to traffic above 150% of committed QPS and expire at quarter-end.
- Usage within the Burst Credit is not subject to retroactive surcharge. Usage beyond the Burst Credit is subject to standard True-Up.
- Price Smoothing for months 1–3: True-Up will use the average effective per-token price across the three months but smoothing excludes permanent volume tier discounts and is capped so the smoothing benefit cannot reduce Redwood's effective realized price by more than 12% compared to the month-1 baseline.
- Contractual guardrails we added: request-level telemetry enabled for spike validation and a reconciliation cap (Redwood undercollection exposure limited to 1.5x the quarter's Burst Credit value; if exceeded, parties get a 30-day remediation window before additional backcharges).

If that looks close to what you need, we can accept these edits into Exhibit B and route for signatures. If Acme prefers a different smoothing cap (e.g., 8–15%), we can discuss tradeoffs; Karthik can provide the worst-case undercollection numbers.

Would you like to review over a 30-minute call tomorrow?

Best —
Dylan
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
